title: Smoked Salmon Sandwich
subtitle: Smoked salmon with cream cheese and capers on brown bread
excerpt: Cold-smoked salmon with cream cheese, capers, red onion, and lemon on brown bread. A British deli counter and afternoon tea classic, ready in 5 minutes with no cooking needed.
sourceNotes: Smoked salmon became a British luxury item in the late nineteenth century, brought by Jewish immigrants from Eastern Europe. By the mid-twentieth century it had become standard for celebration occasions and deli counters. Recipe developed from first principles, based on standard British deli preparations.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 1 hour before serving and keep covered in the fridge. The bread can become moist if left longer.

content.text: Smoked salmon sandwich is cream cheese, cold-smoked salmon, capers, and thinly sliced red onion on brown bread with a squeeze of lemon. There is no cooking: every component goes on cold. The quality of the sandwich depends entirely on the smoked salmon and the freshness of the bread.
Spread {{cream-cheese}} of cream cheese evenly over two slices of {{bread}} brown bread. Butter the other two slices with {{salted-butter}} of butter if using.
Lay {{smoked-salmon}} of smoked salmon in a single layer over the cream cheese. Scatter over {{capers}} of capers and the thinly sliced {{red-onion}} red onion.
Squeeze over a little juice from {{lemon}} and season with black pepper. No salt is needed: the salmon and capers provide plenty.
Close the sandwich, press lightly, and cut in half or into fingers. Serve immediately or keep covered in the fridge for up to 1 hour.

rows.cause: Cheap smoked salmon with high brine content, or capers added without tasting first
rows.fix: Rinse the capers if they are packed in brine rather than oil. Add capers sparingly and taste as you go.

rows.cause: Assembled too far in advance or cream cheese too thin
rows.fix: Cream cheese is a good moisture barrier. Assemble within 1 hour of serving and keep in the fridge.

rows.symptom: Red onion is too sharp and overpowering
rows.cause: Raw red onion is very pungent
rows.fix: Soak the sliced onion in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain and pat dry. This removes much of the harsh bite.

rows.symptom: Salmon slips out when the sandwich is cut
rows.cause: Slices not anchored into the cream cheese
rows.fix: Press the salmon gently into the cream cheese before closing. Cut with a sharp knife in one firm motion rather than sawing.

content.text: Smoked salmon in Britain is closely linked to Jewish deli culture. Eastern European Jewish immigrants brought it to London's East End from the 1880s onwards. The classic pairing of smoked salmon with cream cheese, capers, and onion comes from this tradition. By the second half of the twentieth century, smoked salmon moved into mainstream British food culture. It now appears on hotel menus, at Christmas tables, and at deli counters across the country.
